title: Epochal ingest + dedup for token usage ledger reconciliation
creator: Priya Narang
description:
Background: Our downstream billing ledger occasionally double-counts token usage when retries and replayed events arrive late or when upstream emitters produce duplicate records. Current reconciliation jobs are shard-based and perform expensive full-window scans, causing long tail delays and occasional invoice corrections.

Goal: Implement an epochal ingest layer that partitions raw usage by deterministic ingest epochs (time-window + source-sig) and performs idempotent deduplication before events enter the canonical token ledger. This should reduce reconciliation job runtime by >=50%, cut retroactive invoice adjustments, and simplify per-tenant cost attribution.

Success criteria / acceptance criteria:
- New ingest layer drops >99.9% of exact and near-duplicate events (same request_id or same (tenant,request_fingerprint,seq) within epoch).
- Reconciliation job runtime reduced by >=50% on representative 30-day replay test.
- No material change to billed totals for control tenants during the rollout (<=0.05% variance).
- Safe rollback path that preserves raw events for reprocessing if issues found.

Proposed design (high-level):
1) Ingest service: persist raw events into epoched S3 buckets (or partitioned BigQuery staging) using deterministic epoch key: epoch_start_ts|source_id|shard_mod. Each object contains events + a compact event signature.
2) Dedup worker: run per-epoch distributed dedup using a combination of Bloom filters (for fast negative checks) + a small Redis LRU for hot keys, followed by exact key checks in a strongly consistent store (Dynamo/Spanner) for final de-duplication.
3) Emit canonical events to existing token-ledger topic with a canonical_event_id and source_epoch metadata. Ledger consumers updated to ignore events without canonical_event_id.
4) Migration mode: start with "observe-only" where dedup layer tags events but still forwards originals; run reconciliation comparisons and dashboards. Then switch to "enforce" mode per-tenant via rollout flag.

Trade-offs considered:
- Consistency vs cost: full strong consistency (single authoritative store) is simpler but adds write RPS and cost. Hybrid approach (Bloom+cache+strong final check) chosen to reduce backend RPS while keeping correctness guarantees.
- Storage format: small objects per event increase S3 overhead; we choose batched epoch objects (5K events/object) to balance PUT costs vs tail latency.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Priya Narang: Kickoff notes - confirmed scope with PM (billing team). Confluence draft created: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/TP-epochal-ingest. Asked infra for temporary namespace for dev testing.
2026-03-04 - Ethan Chen: PoC completed for Bloom+Redis pattern. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5234 . PoC shows 87% duplicate drop on sampled noisy tenant data.
2026-03-05 - Miguel Santos (review): Concern about Redis LRU eviction exposing incorrect dedup on bursts. Suggested adding an eviction-safe checkpoint to the strong store every 5 minutes.

2026-03-06 - Ethan Chen: Adjusted design to write strong-store "+pending_index" entries on first-seen, then finalize on epoch close to reduce race windows. Updated design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/TP-epochal-ingest#design-updates.

2026-03-08 - Priya Narang: Data team ran 30-day replay using archived raw events (s3://redwood-raw/replay/2026-02). Reconciliation job runtime dropped from 7h -> 2.5h in observe-only mode. Need further validation on billing delta before can flip enforce for pilot tenants.

2026-03-09 - Security (Anita Kumar): Reviewed approach for canonical_event_id uniqueness and collision resistance. Recommended HMAC with per-tenant key stored in KMS. Added to implementation checklist.

2026-03-10 - Ethan Chen: Created migration runbook and feature-flag gating plan. Runbook link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/epochal-ingest-runbook. Next: pilot with 3 low-risk tenants on 2026-03-18.
runbook: See attachment (Runbook). Key steps: 1) deploy dedup-worker in observe mode, 2) validate reconciliation diffs <0.05% for 72h, 3) enable per-tenant enforce flag for pilot, 4) monitor invoices and alerts for 7 days, 5) promote to cohort rollout and finally global. Rollback: disable enforce flag and reprocess epoch objects. Escalation: page on-call data-engineering and billing-eng slack channels.
notes: Planned rollout: pilot tenants (3), then 10% traffic cohort, 50%, 100%. Estimate assumes infra support for a temporary strong-store table and two weeks of ops monitoring support. Follow-ups: ENG-18402 (housekeeping to retire legacy replay scanners) and ENG-18405 (add per-tenant KMS keys).
